Indicator 2 tracks the proportion of newly diagnosed inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) patients who receive patient education within one year of their diagnosis. This metric is monitored nationally and regionally across Denmark by the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] to evaluate the consistency of post-diagnosis care and patient empowerment [^src1].

Across the Danish regions, there is significant variation in the delivery of this education. [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] leads the country, with 22% of its newly diagnosed patients (142 out of 648) receiving education within the first year [^src1]. In contrast, [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] trails significantly, recording the lowest proportion at just 1% (5 out of 350 patients) [^src1]. The national average for Denmark stands at 13% (331 out of 2,597 patients) [^src1]. 

The remaining regions fall between these extremes but generally hover near or below the national average. [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] achieved a rate of 15% (73 out of 490) [^src1], while [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] reported 10% (89 out of 856) and 9% (22 out of 253), respectively [^src1]. Because this comparison is based on a single reporting period, no longitudinal trends can be established. However, the extreme outlier status of Region Sjælland—scoring a full 12 percentage points below the national average—highlights a stark regional disparity in post-diagnosis patient education [^src1].
